title: Chicken Salteñas (Bolivian Baked Hand Pies)
summary: A juicy chicken, potato, raisin and pea stew set firm by its own reduced wing stock, sealed with egg and olive in a sweet, paprika-tinted dough and baked until golden. Make the filling the day before.
equipment: Dutch oven or large lidded pan
2 baking trays lined with baking paper

ingredients.item: floury potato, peeled and cut into 1 cm dice
fine sea salt or table salt

ingredients.note: boiled 10 min to a firm yolk

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
egg yolk beaten with 1 tbsp water

steps.title: Roast and simmer the wings
steps.text: Heat the oven to 230 °C (210 °C fan) and roast the wings in the tin for 35-40 min until deep golden. Tip them into the saucepan with the water, scrape in the browned bits and simmer, partly covered, for 3 h. The long simmer pulls natural collagen from the skin and joints.

steps.title: Reduce the stock
steps.text: Strain the stock and boil it down to 600 ml. Concentrating the collagen is what lets the filling set firm later, so don't skip this.

steps.title: Stew the chicken
steps.text: Brown the thighs in the oil in the Dutch oven over medium-high heat for 3-4 min a side, then set aside. Lower the heat, soften the onion for 6-8 min, add the garlic, paprika, cumin, oregano and cayenne for 1 min, then the stock, potato, raisins and salt. Return the thighs, cover and simmer gently for 25-30 min until the chicken reaches 74 °C.

steps.title: Chill until set
steps.text: Cool the thighs in the liquid, then chop them small and stir back in with the peas and pepper. Spread in the shallow dish, cover and chill for at least 6 h, ideally overnight, until it sets to a firm, spoonable jelly.

steps.title: Make the dough
steps.text: Melt the butter with the paprika and leave to cool until just warm. Mix the flour, sugar and salt, pour in the butter and rub together, then add the egg and warm water and knead for 3-4 min into a smooth, soft dough. Wrap and rest for 30 min at room temperature so it rolls without shrinking.

steps.title: Fill and seal
steps.text: Divide into 10 balls of about 85 g and roll each to a 15 cm round, 3 mm thick. Add 3 heaped tbsp cold filling, a piece of egg and an olive half, brush the edge with water and fold into a half-moon. Press, then twist the edge over itself to form a rope; a tight seal keeps the juices in.

steps.title: Chill and bake
steps.text: Stand the pies seam up on the trays and chill for 20 min while the oven heats to 200 °C (180 °C fan). Brush with the yolk glaze and bake for 25-30 min until deep golden and the filling is bubbling hot (74 °C). Rest for 10 min, then eat by hand, nibbling a corner first and sipping the juice.

tips: If the filling hasn't set firm, the stock wasn't reduced enough; boil it down further before stewing next time.
A common mistake is filling the pies with warm stew, which melts the dough and leaks; keep the filling fridge-cold.
Hold the salteña upright as you eat so the gravy stays inside.
storage: The set filling keeps in the fridge for 2 days. Baked salteñas keep chilled for 2 days; reheat in a 180 °C (160 °C fan) oven for 12-15 min until piping hot (74 °C). Unbaked, filled pies freeze for 1 month; bake from frozen, adding 10 min. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
